EXISTENCE/SPEC: found SNGPL's (Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd, the actual pipeline owner/operator) own current 'Province-Wise Transmission Breakup' page, a detailed asset table (as of 30 June 2025) listing every named pipeline section by diameter and length. Punjab province lists exactly four 'SUI - MULTAN' rows: 24in/288.06km, 30in/313.78km, 36in/213.68km, 16in/1.85km -- no loop-line-vs-mainline distinction is drawn in that column for these rows (Loop Line KM blank for all four). The 30in/313.78km row is an EXACT match (to 2 decimals) to GEM's P4091 Diameter=30in and LengthKnown=313.78km. Sindh province's table separately lists a 30in SUI-MULTAN segment of 14.29 km (Balochistan's breakdown for the 30in line was ambiguous in the source's rendering, not clearly zero). This confirms the pipeline is REAL, CURRENTLY OPERATING (it is on the operator's live asset table), owned 100% by SNGPL (also confirmed: this is SNGPL's own site), correctly classified as a gas TRANSMISSION line (part of the historic national trunk system, not a gathering/feeder line), and confirms Diameter=30in exactly -- but the LengthKnown figure appears scoped to the Punjab segment only, not the full Sui(Balochistan)-to-Multan(Punjab) route the Start/EndLocation fields imply (see recommendation). Separately consulted SNGPL's own 'History' page, which confirms the Sui-Multan system was taken over by SNGPL at its 1963/64 incorporation (originally 217 mi of 16in + 80 mi of 10in pipe from the Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation) -- this describes the ORIGINAL 1950s/60s-era pipe (pre-dating the 24/30/36in loops that exist today, including this one), so it is background/existence corroboration for the Sui-Multan corridor generally, not a direct spec match for the 30in loop itself. Both SNGPL pages are the SAME origin (pipeline owner's own site) so this is a single-primary-source case, not 2 independent origins; per docs/reference/confidence_tiers.md the rubric explicitly allows tier=high on 'one primary/regulatory source', which this is (the actual asset owner's current network table) -- flagging that basis explicitly rather than claiming false independence. Repeated WebSearch (Bing, DuckDuckGo) attempts to find a second, genuinely separate-origin source for the 30in/313.78km figure specifically were unsuccessful -- 'Sui' collides heavily with Sui-the-blockchain-token in general web search, and OGRA's own site (ogra.org.pk) 403'd to automated fetch. DUPLICATE check against the 63-row Pakistan-gas roster: P4090 (24in/288.06km), P4091 (30in/313.78km, this row), and P4098 (36in/213.68km) are three DIFFERENT diameter pipes on the same Sui-Multan corridor, each independently confirmed against SNGPL's table -- this is a legitimate multi-loop trunk system (mainline + successive capacity loops added over decades), not a duplicate/double-count of P4091.
